flips: UT-01 (Salt Lake City & West Valley City)

summaries.senate: Polymarket odds show the Democrats still favoured to win control of the Senate, though their chances slipped slightly over the past day. The biggest move came in [[Nebraska]], where the Republican Pete Ricketts saw a sharp rise in the odds of holding the seat. In [[Michigan]], the Democrat Abdul El-Sayed gained ground in a sizable way, while in [[Ohio]], Sherrod Brown's chances also moved up by a moderate amount and the market treats the seat as a predicted flip.
summaries.governor: The biggest move came in [[Georgia]], where the Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms gained a sizable amount of ground in what the market treats as a predicted flip. In [[Texas]], the Republican Greg Abbott also strengthened by a sizable margin, as did the Republican Jim Pillen in [[Nebraska]], where the Democrat is Lynne Walz. Elsewhere, the Republican Byron Donalds saw a moderate dip in Florida, where the Democrat is David Jolly.
summaries.house: Polymarket odds show the Democrats favoured to win control of the House, and their chances edged up slightly. In [[NC-13 (Fuquay-Varina & Sanford)]], the Republican Brad Knott saw a sharp drop in chances, while in [[FL-09 (Orlando & Kissimmee)]] the Republican Dan Green slipped by a sizable margin in what the market calls a predicted flip. The Democrat Jamie Ager also lost ground, by a moderate amount, in [[NC-11 (Asheville & Hendersonville)]], another predicted flip.
